newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean gold demand seen slowing in summer.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean gold demand seen slowing in summer.

text.p: South Korean gold demand, already hit by the economic slowdown after a series of corporate collapses, is expected slow further on low seasonal demand, traders said on Tuesday.

They said the domestic bullion market was seen shrugging off reported remarks by Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto that Japan might be tempted to sell U.S. government bonds and switch foreign reserves to gold.
"Domestic gold demand is very scanty due to the usual low demand in summer," a trader with Tong Yang Global said.
The trader said tension on the Korean peninsula, which flared again last week, had eased and failed to boost demand.
Last week, bullion traders said the news that North Korea had warned it was ready for a "final battle" with the United States and South Korea had sparked jitters in all South Korean markets.
"(Now) there is nothing new and fresh in the market," said a dealer with a major trading house.
The trader said the continued influx of smuggled bullion was dragging down domestic gold prices and had dampened demand for legally imported and domestic products.

Domestic gold producer LG Metals' daily selling price for the precious metal, which is regarded as a benchmark for the local bullion wholesale market, fell on Wednesday to 10,110 won per gram from 10,150 won a week ago.
The company's silver price climbed to 154 won a gram from 153 won a week earlier.

The won's telegraphic transfer selling rate for customers, posted by the Korea Exchange Bank, rose slightly on Tuesday to 891.80 per dollar from 892.00 a week earlier. The rate is regarded as a benchmark of local foreign exchange rates for companies.
